items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: He was a West Australian who came over to Melbourne purely and simply because jazz was happening in Melbourne... He's one of the reasons why I, without knowing anything about modern jazz, I don't sort of laugh at it or discard it at all.

ctx.x: Back to Australia, what about Keith Hounslow's band, how do you pronounce that?

Hounslow, that's right. He was a West Australian who came over to Melbourne purely and simply because jazz was happening in Melbourne. And he came over playing early Armstrong type of stuff. He was playing some beautiful music. He was young, keen. Gradually he changed. He's now playing the most far out modern jazz that anyone is playing in Australia. But he's playing hot modern jazz, which is good. And he's still prepared to have a go at things, even if he makes a mistake or two. He's one of the reasons why I,…
And is there much modern jazz over there? Is that a big competition? Not very much.
